events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 7 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The meter billed the rider over the shortest-and-most-direct route: GPS shows 24.4 km actually driven against a 21.2 km optimal route, +3.2 km (+15%), and the fare shows the excess distance was billed at $4.51 (3.20 km × $1.4101/km). [F1 F4 F6] [RD-1 RD-2]
C2: One off-route segment (09:24–09:30) added 3.07 km: 3.78 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, and the car was up to 688 m off the optimal route; this is a single unexcused detour for the purposes of RD-1. [F3] [RD-1]
C3: This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the detour distance directly entered the fare; RD-2 requires a partial refund measured as the unexcused segment's extra_km × the trip's per-km rate, i.e. 3.07 km × $1.4101/km = $4.33 (rounded to the cent). [F4 F6 F3] [RD-2]
C4: The driver offers no traffic excuse: there were no traffic incidents near the route in the trip window, the only band records (East Coast Parkway, Airport Boulevard, both band 5 = 40–49 km/h) are mid-range and at best corroborative and cannot exempt the segment on their own, and the weather was fine, 0.0 mm rain. [F13 F11 F12 F14] [RD-4]
C5: No consent covers the segment: the complete, fully timestamped chat record contains only the rider's pickup note (09:04) and the driver's car description (09:05) — nothing before the 09:24 segment start in which the rider agreed to any route, general or named, so the deviation was unilateral. [F7 F8 F9] [RD-5]
C6: The driver's post-trip statement 'I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted' is not consent and is not traffic evidence; it is contradicted by the GPS record of a 688 m maximum deviation, and Ryde's own rule allows a driver to pick a quicker route only where the parties agree beforehand. [F10 F3] [RD-5 RD-4]
C7: The rider asked for the excess-distance refund within the trip and the driver's 90-day record shows 1 upheld dispute, but that upheld dispute is a no-show matter (route: 0), so it does not make this case 'repeated' for route purposes and I do not press a flag_account request on that basis. [F16 F15] [RD-6]
Weaknesses: The detour is unexcused under RD-4 only because F13 records no incidents; the driver will argue the recorded band-5 speeds on the optimal corridor (F11, F12) show congestion on the route anyway, and he may lean on RD-4(b) as corroboration. | The refund is limited by RD-2: it covers only the unexcused segment's extra_km, so the remainder of the 3.2 km excess (F1: +3.2 km vs F3: 3.07 km, a ~0.13 km difference) is not refundable, and the driver will point to that gap. | The driver will rely on F10's claim that the GPS rerouted him and on the absence of any rider message objecting during the trip; the rider's complaint that the driver 'turned off the route without a word' rests on a chat record (F7–F9) that shows no route discussion at all, so the rider's own account of the exchange is not corroborated by any message. | The per-km rate used for the calculation comes from F4/F6 (distance fare ÷ distance km); Ryde has not published the RydeTAXI unit rate (G10), so the driver may dispute the exact figure even though it is the only rate derivable from the fare facts.
Asks: refund_partial $4.33

claims.assertion: The meter billed the rider over the shortest-and-most-direct route: GPS shows 24.4 km actually driven against a 21.2 km optimal route, +3.2 km (+15%), and the fare shows the excess distance was billed at $4.51 (3.20 km × $1.4101/km).

One off-route segment (09:24–09:30) added 3.07 km: 3.78 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, and the car was up to 688 m off the optimal route; this is a single unexcused detour for the purposes of RD-1.

This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the detour distance directly entered the fare; RD-2 requires a partial refund measured as the unexcused segment's extra_km × the trip's per-km rate, i.e. 3.07 km × $1.4101/km = $4.33 (rounded to the cent).

The driver offers no traffic excuse: there were no traffic incidents near the route in the trip window, the only band records (East Coast Parkway, Airport Boulevard, both band 5 = 40–49 km/h) are mid-range and at best corroborative and cannot exempt the segment on their own, and the weather was fine, 0.0 mm rain.

No consent covers the segment: the complete, fully timestamped chat record contains only the rider's pickup note (09:04) and the driver's car description (09:05) — nothing before the 09:24 segment start in which the rider agreed to any route, general or named, so the deviation was unilateral.

The driver's post-trip statement 'I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted' is not consent and is not traffic evidence; it is contradicted by the GPS record of a 688 m maximum deviation, and Ryde's own rule allows a driver to pick a quicker route only where the parties agree beforehand.

The rider asked for the excess-distance refund within the trip and the driver's 90-day record shows 1 upheld dispute, but that upheld dispute is a no-show matter (route: 0), so it does not make this case 'repeated' for route purposes and I do not press a flag_account request on that basis.

weaknesses: The detour is unexcused under RD-4 only because F13 records no incidents; the driver will argue the recorded band-5 speeds on the optimal corridor (F11, F12) show congestion on the route anyway, and he may lean on RD-4(b) as corroboration.

The refund is limited by RD-2: it covers only the unexcused segment's extra_km, so the remainder of the 3.2 km excess (F1: +3.2 km vs F3: 3.07 km, a ~0.13 km difference) is not refundable, and the driver will point to that gap.

The driver will rely on F10's claim that the GPS rerouted him and on the absence of any rider message objecting during the trip; the rider's complaint that the driver 'turned off the route without a word' rests on a chat record (F7–F9) that shows no route discussion at all, so the rider's own account of the exchange is not corroborated by any message.

The per-km rate used for the calculation comes from F4/F6 (distance fare ÷ distance km); Ryde has not published the RydeTAXI unit rate (G10), so the driver may dispute the exact figure even though it is the only rate derivable from the fare facts.

claims.assertion: The meter billed the rider over the shortest-and-most-direct route: GPS shows 24.4 km actually driven against a 21.2 km optimal route, +3.2 km (+15%), and the fare shows the excess distance was billed at $4.51 (3.20 km × $1.4101/km).

One off-route segment (09:24–09:30) added 3.07 km: 3.78 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, and the car was up to 688 m off the optimal route; this is a single unexcused detour for the purposes of RD-1.

This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the detour distance directly entered the fare; RD-2 requires a partial refund measured as the unexcused segment's extra_km × the trip's per-km rate, i.e. 3.07 km × $1.4101/km = $4.33 (rounded to the cent).

The driver offers no traffic excuse: there were no traffic incidents near the route in the trip window, the only band records (East Coast Parkway, Airport Boulevard, both band 5 = 40–49 km/h) are mid-range and at best corroborative and cannot exempt the segment on their own, and the weather was fine, 0.0 mm rain.

No consent covers the segment: the complete, fully timestamped chat record contains only the rider's pickup note (09:04) and the driver's car description (09:05) — nothing before the 09:24 segment start in which the rider agreed to any route, general or named, so the deviation was unilateral.

The driver's post-trip statement 'I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted' is not consent and is not traffic evidence; it is contradicted by the GPS record of a 688 m maximum deviation, and Ryde's own rule allows a driver to pick a quicker route only where the parties agree beforehand.

The rider asked for the excess-distance refund within the trip and the driver's 90-day record shows 1 upheld dispute, but that upheld dispute is a no-show matter (route: 0), so it does not make this case 'repeated' for route purposes and I do not press a flag_account request on that basis.

weaknesses: The detour is unexcused under RD-4 only because F13 records no incidents; the driver will argue the recorded band-5 speeds on the optimal corridor (F11, F12) show congestion on the route anyway, and he may lean on RD-4(b) as corroboration.

The refund is limited by RD-2: it covers only the unexcused segment's extra_km, so the remainder of the 3.2 km excess (F1: +3.2 km vs F3: 3.07 km, a ~0.13 km difference) is not refundable, and the driver will point to that gap.

The driver will rely on F10's claim that the GPS rerouted him and on the absence of any rider message objecting during the trip; the rider's complaint that the driver 'turned off the route without a word' rests on a chat record (F7–F9) that shows no route discussion at all, so the rider's own account of the exchange is not corroborated by any message.

The per-km rate used for the calculation comes from F4/F6 (distance fare ÷ distance km); Ryde has not published the RydeTAXI unit rate (G10), so the driver may dispute the exact figure even though it is the only rate derivable from the fare facts.

claims.assertion: There is exactly one off-route segment: 09:24–09:30, where 3.78 km was driven against 0.71 km on the optimal route, adding 3.07 km (F3). Every other metre of the +3.2 km difference (F1) sits in the 200 m route corridor and is map-matching noise, which RD-2 expressly excludes from refund.

The rider's own complaint is confined to 'the extra distance' and the meter reading (F1, F6); no published surcharge was added — waiting is $0.00 and the platform fee $1.47 is a published fee (F6), so FARE-1 yields nothing beyond the mileage calculation.

If any refund is ordered, it is the mileage-only amount on the single unexempted segment: 3.07 km × $1.4101/km (F4, F6) = $4.33, which is the maximum exposure; the excess distance billed is $4.51 (F4).

The driver did not conceal the diversion: he sent no claim of agreement in chat (F7, F8, F9) and his post-trip statement is that the navigation rerouted him (F10); there is no rider consent message because there was no agreed route change.

The traffic record does not excuse the segment on its own: no incidents were recorded near the route (F13), and the only speed bands on the optimal corridor were band 5, 40–49 km/h, on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard (F11, F12) — well outside the band 1/2 severe-congestion definition in RD-4(b), which cannot exempt a segment in any event.

No safety escalation is warranted: there is no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere in the chat or the driver's statement (F7, F8, F10), and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F14).

The driver's record should not be aggravated: his one upheld dispute in 90 days is a no-show, not a route finding (route: 0) (F16), so the RD-6 recidivism condition (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met and no flag_account should attach.

weaknesses: The system records clearly contradict the driver's statement (F10): F3 records a concrete 3.07 km off-route segment, F1 records +3.2 km (+15%) against the optimal route, and F2 records +8.4 minutes of extra driving — so the assertion that 'the GPS made me do it' cannot defeat RD-1, and under RD-4(c) the segment falls to RD-2.

The single-segment argument is weak against the other side's obvious use of F1: the rider will say +3.2 km total (F1) should be refunded at the per-km rate (F4), i.e. $4.51, rather than the $4.33 we concede from F3, and RD-2's corridor/noise exclusion is derived, not Ryde-published (vacancy G5).
There is no consent evidence at all: chat shows only greeting/position messages (F7, F8, F9) and the driver's statement claims no agreement (F10), so RD-5 gives no cover for the 09:24–09:30 segment.
The driver's own profile history (F16, 2 disputes, 1 upheld) invites the rider to press for account review, even though the upheld item is a no-show and RD-6's route-specific threshold is not met.

notices.text:
Good news: we're refunding $4.33 to you.

Our records show one part of your trip where the driver went off the best route — about 3.07 km further than needed. That extra distance was added to your metered fare, so you paid for it.

We're not refunding the rest of the extra distance, because only that off-route stretch can be refunded under our rules, and it's 3.07 km at your trip's rate.

The $4.33 comes as a Ryde voucher on your account. No action needed from you.

Your driver's file has been noted.

Thanks for flagging it.

We've looked at this trip and found one off-route stretch: about 3.07 km driven beyond the best route, which added to the rider's metered fare.

We're not treating it as an approved detour. There was no traffic incident recorded near the route, and the chat doesn't show the rider agreeing to a route or a stop.

So the trip is being refunded $4.33 to the rider as a Ryde voucher, and this is recorded on your file. Your account isn't being flagged, and you can keep driving as normal.

If you think the GPS routed you differently, tell us and we'll look again.
